question.text: A donor asks the SIA (during a post-SIR Q&A) to confirm which fund qualifies for 100% deduction WITHOUT any qualifying-limit under Section 80G. Which option is correct?

answer.text: Donation to a local authority for family planning — 100% deduction without limit
Donation to Indira Gandhi Memorial Fund — 100% deduction without limit
Donation to a Section 8 FPE on the SSE — 100% deduction without limit
Donation to Prime Minister's National Relief Fund — 100% deduction without any qualifying limit

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The chapter explicitly classifies Prime Minister's National Relief Fund, PM CARES Fund, National Defence Fund, National Foundation for Communal Harmony, and National/State Blood Transfusion Councils as '100% deduction without any qualifying limit' under Section 80G. Family-planning donations to local authorities are 100% but subject to the 10% AGTI cap. The Indira Gandhi Memorial Fund is in the 50% WITHOUT limit bucket. SSE-listed FPEs do NOT automatically get 80G — the FPE must separately register, and even then only the NPO side gets 80G status. **The Trap:** Family-planning donations fall in the 100% WITH 10% AGTI cap category. Indira Gandhi Memorial Fund is 50% (not 100%). Section 8 FPEs are NOT automatic 80G beneficiaries. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A (MF Distributor), X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) test 80G category tables. XXIII focuses on how the SIA presents these distinctions to donors during the impact-report communication. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Keep a pre-printed '80G 4-bucket chart' ready in your SIA working papers: (i) 100% no limit, (ii) 50% no limit, (iii) 100% with 10% AGTI cap, (iv) 50% with 10% AGTI cap. When you see the SE marketing materials promise 100% deduction, cross-check the fund type before signing off — misleading 80G claims are a reputational risk.
